item.title: Research Papers Dataset
item.description: How and why I built the research papers dataset.

item.title: what am I actually looking at in a model map?
item.description: I want a human-readable model microscope, but every pretty node and edge should tell me whether it is structure, an observed activation or something I've actually tested causally.

item.title: xanadu-2: links that remember what they point to
item.description: Normal links point somewhere. I'm interested in links that also remember which version and exact passage I meant when I created them.

item.title: sorting old notes without rewriting history
item.description: A research folder turns into an archaeological site surprisingly fast. I want a clean reading copy without losing the weird history that explains where it came from.

item.title: knowledge bases should help me choose the next check
item.description: I don't really need a knowledge base to remember every term. I want it to help me work out what to inspect next and what that check can actually tell me.

item.title: an embedding column needs more than a convincing name
item.description: Before I trust an embedding search or scatterplot, I want to know exactly which model produced the vectors, how they were made and whether the query uses the same representation.

item.title: doing research without losing the question
item.description: I like weird questions. The trick is stopping one question from becoming a reading list, dashboard and three architectures before I decide what would count as an answer.

item.title: making synthetic data I can actually check
item.description: Generating another thousand examples is easy. I care more about whether I can independently check why each one survived the pipeline.

item.title: a readable PDF export can still be wrong
item.description: PDF conversion can look finished long before I've checked whether the Markdown still means the same thing as the original page.

item.title: collecting papers without losing why I wanted them
item.description: I can build a reading queue much faster than I can read it. The useful part is remembering why something went into the queue and which version I actually meant.

item.title: cleaning a dataset without cleaning away its meaning
item.description: I want dataset cleanup to remove repetitive work, not quietly decide that IDs are numbers, casing never matters or conflicting duplicates can be thrown away.

item.title: pulling useful fields out of messy text
item.description: Turning messy text into a clean table is easy to demo. The harder part is making sure every neat little cell still has evidence behind it.

item.title: image conversion has more edge cases than the button suggests
item.description: “Make this image smaller” sounds simple until smaller could mean fewer pixels, fewer bytes, a square canvas or just something that uploads properly.

item.title: getting a useful export out of a chat log
item.description: A chat export becomes useful when I can trace a cleaned field or spreadsheet row all the way back to the exact message that produced it.

item.title: minecraft time with astra
item.description: Spent some time playing around with Astra during the last few days and gave it my usual Minecraft test. I know these oneshot game clones have been benchmarked to death, but I still find them…

item.title: botsim: letting the locals talk
item.description: I like the idea of leaving a tiny local community of model personas running, then seeing what survives once scheduling, memory and interruptions get in the way.
